messages:
maya: heads-up — we're seeing a small wave of read errors on ephemeral NVMe in us-east1-c, started ~00:18 UTC. GPU attaches stalled for a few minutes. metric spike: nvme_read_retries and janitor_evictions.

jordan: ugh. any pattern on instance flavor or zone subset?

maya: looks concentrated on g4x nodes in rack b7. not all g4x though. 3 hosts with repeated read-retry counts.

li: can you paste the node ids? i'll pull smart and dmesg.

maya: gnode-ue1b7-023, gnode-ue1b7-045, gnode-ue1b7-067

ash: @li FYI janitor daemons on those hosts were performing a high-concurrency vacuum between 00:10-00:16. Could be io contention causing firmware retries.

li: pulled logs from gnode-ue1b7-023:

```:
[  412.345678] nvme0: retrying R/W command, status: 0x2
[  412.345689] nvme0n1: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[  413.101234] nvme: drv: reset controller
```

smartctl shows rising media errors but not critical yet.

jordan: any recent firmware pushes to that cohort?

maya: none in the last 2 weeks. last maint window was 9 days ago (thermal sensor thresholds tweak).

sre-bot: auto-alert: GPU-ATTACH-HOLD triggered for us-east1-c (3 hosts) — auto-mitigation: 2 minute attach backoff enforced.

ash: ok mitigation idea — throttle janitor concurrency on that rack and try a soft nvme reset via maintenance script. but we should avoid mass reboots.

li: agree. i'll run a targeted reset and drop janitor concurrency to 1 for affected hosts. command I'll run:

```:
ssh root@gnode-ue1b7-023 -- "echo 1 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/device/reset"
systemctl stop janitor-worker && export JANITOR_CONCURRENCY=1 && systemctl start janitor-worker
```

maya: noted. please run on 023 first, watch attach success rate.

li: doing it now.

li: done on 023 — saw immediate drop in read_retries, gpu attach succeeded for queued pods. 045 still noisy.

jordan: can we patch janitor to backoff more aggressively on persistent retries? Seems like simultaneous scrub + heavy kvcache writes equals oscillation.

ash: long term yes — Optimize janitor to check NVMe retry counters before spawning heavy passes. Short term, lowering concurrency + soft reset should help.

sre-bot: monitoring: after action, nvme_read_retries on 023 dropped from 120/min -> 4/min. 045 still at ~90/min.

li: prepping to run reset on 045/067 in staggered windows 2m apart.

maya: do it. coordinate with scheduler so we don't hit attach storm.

ops-bot: scheduled maintenance: staggered resets queued at 00:32, 00:34 UTC.

li: resets done. 045 normalized, 067 showed residual media errors; reimaged a small shard and drained for further observation.

jordan: cost question — if we see recurring wear like this on rack b7, should we reserve replacement drives vs. increasing janitor throttles? Replacement vs operational overhead.

ash: short term cheaper to tune janitor/backoff. medium term if SMART error rates trend upward across >5% of nodes in a cohort, escalate to procurement for replacements. keep replacement threshold documented.

maya: opened follow-up ticket (#INF-4821) to track SMART trends and set automated cohort-level alerts.

li: added a quick kpi card to console: nvme_read_retries per-rack + janitor_concurrency. will link in the ticket.

maya: thanks. summary: targeted soft resets + janitor concurrency=1 cleared immediate stalls. ongoing: monitor SMART trend on b7, consider replacements if errors persist. closing here unless new noise.

ash: :thumbsup:

jordan: nice triage team. low-friction fix for now.

sre-bot: incident closed (monitoring mode) — will reopen if gpu-attach-hold re-triggers.
